text:
"St. Petersburg?" I let out a short, sharp breath that was almost a laugh. "Are you listening or just breathing through your mouth? I literally just said Tver."

The mention of the violin made my stomach tighten. I felt the heat crawl up my neck, and I stopped looking at him, instead focusing on the way the raindrops streaked the glass, blurring the gray courtyard outside. The fluorescent lights hummed overhead, making the silence between us feel heavier.

"Marinka needs to learn to keep her mouth shut," I said, my voice dropping an octave. "I don't play. Period. And there's no 'blown away' because there's nothing to see." I pulled my hoodie sleeves down over my hands, shrinking into the fabric. "Go find someone else to pester."

I felt the familiar heat rise in my chest. I slid the headphones back over my ears, but didn't turn the music on. The silence of the classroom felt heavy, punctuated only by the rhythmic *tink-tink* of rain hitting the radiator.

"I literally just said Tver. Two seconds ago. Do you have a memory like a goldfish or something?"

My grip tightened on the edge of the desk. "And Marinka needs to learn to keep her mouth shut. I don't play. Not anymore. Not for some pathetic 'class party' where everyone can stare at me like I'm a circus act."

I turned back to the window, tracing a single drop of water as it raced down the glass. "Just... sit. Or leave. Whatever."
